name: Tuna and Egg Briks
assumptions: Recipe makes 8 briks as explicitly stated in the instructions (one heaped tbsp filling per brik, repeated to make 8 in all).
Preparation and cooking time summed from instructions: ~10 min for spring onions/spinach, ~5 min cooling/drain, ~5 min assembly of 8 briks, 12-15 min bake; total conservatively 35 min.
Tuna is a fish; eggs are eggs; no milk, shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, soy, or sesame listed.
Spinach, tomatoes, cucumber, lemon juice, olive oil, spring onions, hot sauce, and apricot jam introduce no listed allergens.
No dairy ingredients present (apricot jam is fruit-based).
Not vegetarian (tuna) or vegan (tuna and eggs).
instructions:
Heat 2 tsp of the oil in a large saucepan and cook the spring onions over a low heat for 3 minutes or until beginning to soften. Add the spinach, cover with a tight-fitting lid and cook for a further 2–3 minutes or until tender and wilted, stirring once or twice. Tip the mixture into a sieve or colander and leave to drain and cool.
Using a saucer as a guide, cut out 24 rounds about 12.5 cm (5 in) in diameter from the filo pastry, cutting 6 rounds from each sheet. Stack the filo rounds in a pile, then cover with cling film to prevent them from drying out.
When the spinach mixture is cool, squeeze out as much excess liquid as possible, then transfer to a bowl. Add the tuna, eggs, hot pepper sauce, and salt and pepper to taste. Mix well.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F, gas mark 6). Take one filo round and very lightly brush with some of the remaining oil. Top with a second round and brush with a little oil, then place a third round on top and brush with oil.
Place a heaped tbsp of the filling in the middle of the round, then fold the pastry over to make a half-moon shape. Fold in the edges, twisting them to seal, and place on a non-stick baking sheet. Repeat with the remaining pastry and filling to make 8 briks in all.
Lightly brush the briks with the remaining oil. Bake for 12–15 minutes or until the pastry is crisp and golden brown.
Meanwhile, combine the tomatoes and cucumber in a bowl and sprinkle with the lemon juice and seasoning to taste. Serve the briks hot with this salad and the chutney.

ingredients.name: Olive Oil
ingredients.assumptions: 2 tbs olive oil (standard 14g per tbsp, total 28g rounded; used for cooking and brushing, typical extra virgin olive oil values

ingredients.name: Spring Onions
ingredients.assumptions: 8 spring onions, average 15g each trimmed (typical bunch portion used in recipes)

ingredients.name: Spinach
ingredients.assumptions: 200g fresh spinach as listed, raw values (wilted and drained in recipe, but base nutrition on supplied weight)

ingredients.name: Filo Pastry
ingredients.assumptions: 4 standard sheets filo pastry (~70g per full sheet, total 280g; recipe uses 24 rounds cut from them, entire sheets included)

ingredients.name: Tuna
ingredients.assumptions: 1 standard can tuna in water/brine (drained weight ~140g typical for 185g can; recipe context implies drained tuna)

ingredients.name: Eggs
ingredients.assumptions: 2 large eggs (~50g each without shell, typical large egg edible portion)

ingredients.name: Hotsauce
ingredients.assumptions: Dash of hot pepper sauce (plausible small recipe amount ~5g; negligible macros)

ingredients.name: Tomatoes
ingredients.assumptions: 4 medium tomatoes chopped (~125g each, typical medium tomato weight)

ingredients.name: Cucumber
ingredients.assumptions: 1/4 large cucumber (~300g whole typical, so 75g portion)

ingredients.name: Lemon Juice
ingredients.assumptions: 1 tbs lemon juice (standard 15g volume, typical fresh lemon juice values)

ingredients.name: Apricot Jam
ingredients.assumptions: 4 tbs apricot jam (standard 20g per tbsp, total 80g; typical fruit jam values)
